claims.text: The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ ('Output value errors') exists and covers this and other symptoms of treating a Pulumi output as if it were already a plain value.

When a Pulumi Output<T> is treated as a plain value (e.g., string-interpolated or logged), the resulting text contains placeholder text like 'Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported' instead of the actual value.
The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ exists and covers diagnosing errors from stringifying, branching on, or reading a Pulumi output value as if it were a plain value.

Pulumi Cloud returns a "409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress" error when another update is already running on a stack, and the update-conflicts troubleshooting page covers resolving it.
The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists.
Pulumi Cloud can return 500 internal server errors, and the page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/server-errors/ exists to handle them.
The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/post-step-errors/ exists and covers post-step event failures and engine bugs.
The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/connection-issues/ exists and covers network connectivity and proxy problems.

The Pulumi CLI produces a `read ".pulumi/meta.yaml"` error when it cannot access a self-managed (DIY) state backend, and the DIY backend page has an anchor #error-reading-pulumimetayaml describing it.
The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ exists and covers scenarios when `pulumi destroy` fails.
The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/interrupted-updates/ exists and covers recovering from interrupted deployments.
On Apple Silicon Macs, running x86_64 Pulumi binaries under Rosetta 2 can cause crashes or hangs, and the architecture-mismatch page exists and covers fixing them.
The page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/troubleshooting/ exists and covers CI/CD pipeline issues.
The page /docs/iac/operations/stack-management/editing-state-files/ exists and describes safe techniques for modifying Pulumi state files.
A recently deleted stack can be recovered from the Pulumi Cloud console, including after an accidental `pulumi stack rm --force`.
Pulumi supports limiting operations to specific resources with the `--target` and `--exclude` flags (targeted updates).
The Pulumi logging documentation covers automatic logging, CLI verbose logging, and program logging.
Pulumi provides pre-release dev builds that can be installed to access bug fixes not yet shipped in a stable release.
Running `pulumi logs share` securely sends the logs from a failed operation to the Pulumi team.
The logging guide has an #automatic-logging anchor that covers the `pulumi logs share` command.
Pulumi has a Community Slack at slack.pulumi.com that provides community support.
A guide for filing GitHub issues exists at /docs/support/filing-issues/.
Pulumi offers paid support options via its contact page.
The update-conflicts troubleshooting page relates to GitHub issue pulumi/pulumi#20846 and replaces the old #conflict anchor on this page.
The verbose logging content moved to /docs/iac/operations/debugging/logging/#cli-verbose-logging (pulumi/docs#16985), replacing the old #verbose-logging anchor.
Pulumi resource properties are represented as Outputs rather than plain values because their real values are not known until the resource providing them has been created or updated.
Representing resource properties as Outputs is central to how Pulumi builds a dependency graph and runs `pulumi preview`.

Converting a Pulumi output value to a string directly (concatenating, logging) instead of using `apply` or an equivalent helper does not raise an error by default; Pulumi silently substitutes a placeholder message in place of the value.

In the Pulumi TypeScript SDK, interpolating an output (e.g. `${bucket.bucketName}`) into a template string produces a string containing text like `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `apply` or `pulumi.interpolate`, and throws no exception.

In the Pulumi TypeScript SDK, calling `JSON.stringify()` on an output, or letting one flow into a JSON body, produces a `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` string rather than the value.

In the Pulumi Python SDK, formatting an Output in an f-string produces a string containing text like `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported`, and Pulumi also logs a warning; no exception is raised.
In the Pulumi Python SDK, passing an Output to `json.dumps()` fails with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`.
The Pulumi Python SDK provides `Output.json_dumps()` for serializing outputs to JSON.
In Pulumi Go, passing a `pulumi.StringOutput` where a `string` is expected is a compile error, and values are resolved inside `ApplyT`.

In the Pulumi C# SDK, interpolating an output into a string produces text like `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `Apply` or `Output.Format`, and throws no exception.

Setting the environment variable `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true` (supported in TypeScript, Python, and C#) makes converting an output to a string throw an exception at the point of the mistake instead of returning the placeholder text.
Pulumi provides `pulumi.interpolate` and `pulumi.concat` in TypeScript as string-composition helpers for outputs.
Pulumi provides `Output.concat`, `Output.format`, and `Output.json_dumps` in Python as string-composition helpers for outputs.
Pulumi provides `pulumi.Sprintf` and `pulumi.JSONMarshal` in Go as helpers for composing strings/JSON from outputs.
Pulumi provides `Output.Format` in C# as a string-composition helper for outputs.
Pages exist at /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/apply/ and /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/all/ covering accessing single outputs with apply and working with multiple outputs.
A docs page exists at /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/ with an #outputs section.

A value read inside an `apply` callback is only available inside that callback (or in another output derived from it); assigning it to an outer variable and using it outside the callback yields undefined because the callback runs asynchronously after the program's top-level code finishes.
The `apply` callback runs when the Pulumi engine resolves the dependency graph, not on the program's clock, so adding a delay does not fix the ordering problem.
Most Pulumi resource inputs accept outputs as well as plain values, so an output can be passed directly as an input without `apply`.

In a dynamically typed language, an `if` on a Pulumi output evaluates the output object itself (generally always true) rather than its eventual value; in a statically typed language this is usually a compile error because `Output<bool>` is not a `bool`.
A value known when the program starts, such as a stack configuration setting read with `pulumi.Config`, an environment variable, or a hardcoded flag, is a plain value and can be branched on normally.
When a branch depends on a resource's output, the branch must move inside `apply`, deriving a new Output whose value depends on the branch.
Passing an output as a resource's logical name or as a loop bound or map key fails to compile in TypeScript, Go, and C#, where these positions are typed as plain strings or numbers.
In the Pulumi Python SDK, passing an output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string`.
In Python, using a Pulumi output as a loop bound (`range(some_output)`) raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.
In Python, using a Pulumi output as a dictionary key does not raise an error; Python falls back to comparing and hashing the output object itself, so the lookup silently keys on the wrong thing.

When resource names or counts depend on data only known after a resource is created, one fix is to provision dependent resources in a later, separate stack that consumes the first stack's outputs through a StackReference.
A docs page exists at /docs/iac/concepts/stacks/ with a #stackreferences section.

Pulumi has no supported way to block the program and synchronously pull a resolved value out of an output; awaiting or synchronously reading an output either doesn't compile, fails at runtime, or returns placeholder text.
`pulumi stack output <name>` reads a single stack output from the CLI after a deployment.
The Pulumi Automation API exposes an `outputs` field on the result of running an update (e.g. `res.Outputs` in Go).
A docs page exists at /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/.
